classification.difficultyReason: Model successive transfers with two symbolic starting volumes, reduce final equality to a relationship between them and interpret its ratio.

content.prompt: One jug contains $x$ litres of water. A second jug contains $y$ litres of water. Half the contents of the first jug are transferred into the second jug then one third of the contents of the second jug are transferred to the first jug. After which the two jugs contain the same amount of water. Solve for $\frac{x}{y}$. Interpret your answer.

answer.short:
$\frac{x}{y}=1$. The two jugs must initially contain the same volume of water.

Equate their contents after both transfers.
answer.worked:
After the first transfer, the jugs contain $\frac{x}{2}$ and $y+\frac{x}{2}$ litres. After the second transfer, their contents are $\frac{x}{2}+\frac13(y+\frac{x}{2})$ and $\frac23(y+\frac{x}{2})$ litres.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{x}{2}+\frac13\left(y+\frac{x}{2}\right)&=\frac23\left(y+\frac{x}{2}\right)\\3x+2\left(y+\frac{x}{2}\right)&=4\left(y+\frac{x}{2}\right)\\4x+2y&=2x+4y\\2x&=2y\\x&=y\\\frac{x}{y}&=1\end{align*}$$
The two jugs must initially contain the same volume of water.
